title: HTML background images: legacy patterns and CSS migration
learningObjectives: Explain html background images: legacy patterns and css migration and its role in modern HTML.
Select the correct elements, attributes, APIs, or browser behaviour for a practical use case.
Distinguish current practices from obsolete, limited, or legacy techniques.
Build and inspect a working example while considering accessibility and maintainability.
Diagnose common implementation errors and explain the trade-offs of the chosen approach.

understand.concept: Background imagery is presentation, not document content. Older HTML examples may use obsolete body background attributes or similar presentational techniques. Modern pages use CSS background-image and related properties such as background-repeat, background-position, background-size, background-attachment, and the background shorthand. If an image conveys information, use an img element with appropriate alternative text instead of hiding that information in a CSS background. Background images may need overlays, fallback colours, responsive alternatives, and careful contrast.
understand.whyItMatters: Learners must recognize legacy examples while choosing maintainable, responsive CSS for current projects. The distinction between informative content images and decorative backgrounds is essential for accessibility.
understand.analogy: A background image is wallpaper; a content image is an illustration that the reader is expected to understand.
understand.analogyLimit: Some background images communicate meaning in context, so the wallpaper comparison cannot replace an accessibility decision.

explain.narrative: Migrate a legacy background attribute to a CSS class. Then control sizing, positioning, repetition, and fallback colour without changing the semantic HTML.

examples.explanation: The section uses a CSS background. The fallback colour remains visible if the image fails, and cover fills the region while preserving the image's aspect ratio.
examples.expectedOutput: A hero region with a centered cover background and readable white heading; hero.webp must exist.

examples.explanation: A decorative repeating pattern is kept out of the accessibility tree because it carries no information. Do not use aria-hidden on meaningful content.
examples.expectedOutput: A region with a repeating decorative SVG pattern.

practise.guidedTask: Replace an obsolete HTML background attribute with CSS. Add a fallback colour, choose cover or contain deliberately, and test the result at three viewport widths.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive hero that keeps heading contrast readable over variable imagery. Provide a separate content image with alt text when the image itself communicates information.
hints: Use CSS for backgrounds; avoid obsolete presentational HTML attributes.
Use img with alt text for meaningful content imagery.
background-size: cover can crop important parts of an image; test the focal point.

questions.prompt: Where should a modern background image be declared?
questions.explanation: CSS is the modern presentation mechanism for background imagery.

questions.prompt: When should an image usually be an img element rather than a CSS background?
options: When the image conveys content that needs an alternative text
Whenever it is used as wallpaper
Only when the image is a gradient
questions.answer: When the image conveys content that needs an alternative text
questions.explanation: Meaningful content images need text alternatives; decorative backgrounds generally do not.

options: Scales the image to cover the box, possibly cropping it
Makes the image an HTML link
questions.answer: Scales the image to cover the box, possibly cropping it
questions.explanation: Cover preserves aspect ratio while filling the box, so cropping may occur.

options: The colour remains available if the image cannot load
It makes the image file smaller
questions.answer: The colour remains available if the image cannot load
questions.explanation: Fallback colour prevents an empty or unreadable region when the image fails.

questions.prompt: Which property controls where a background image is positioned?
questions.explanation: background-position sets the image's alignment within its background positioning area.
